papers.title: Efficiency of active learning for the allocation of workers on crowdsourced classification tasks
papers.abstract: Crowdsourcing has been successfully employed in the past as an effective and cheap way to execute classification tasks and has therefore attracted the attention of the research community. However, we still lack a theoretical understanding of how to collect the labels from the crowd in an optimal way. In this paper we focus on the problem of worker allocation and compare two active learning policies proposed in the empirical literature with a uniform allocation of the available budget. To this end we make a thorough mathematical analysis of the problem and derive a new bound on the performance of the system. Furthermore we run extensive simulations in a more realistic scenario and show that our theoretical results hold in practice.

summary_en.motivation: To highlight the inherent limitations of using volumetric energy density as a sole design parameter for selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: The study systematically varies process parameters and analyzes their effects on melt pool characteristics and part quality.
summary_en.result: It demonstrates that volumetric energy density alone cannot account for the complex interplay of laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of density and defect formation under different parameter sets support the findings.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the influence of scan direction, part placement, and inert gas flow velocity on the tensile strength of AlSi10Mg components fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: A designed experiment varying these process parameters was conducted, followed by tensile testing to correlate parameters with mechanical performance.
summary_en.result: Scan direction and gas flow velocity were found to significantly affect tensile strength, while part placement had a lesser impact.

papers.title: Two-dimensional simulation of grain structure growth within selective laser melted AA-2024
papers.abstract: The developed Cellular Automata -Finite Element model accurately predicts the microstructure of components manufactured via Selective Laser Melting. The developed Finite Element model accurately predicts the melt pool size in the Selective Laser Melting Process. Cooling and solidification rates are calculated with help of the developed Finite Element model.

papers.title: Optical design of f-theta lens for dual wavelength selective laser melting
papers.abstract: F-theta lens is an important unit for selective laser melting (SLM) manufacture. The dual wavelength f-theta lens has not been used in SLM manufacture. Here, we present the design of the f-theta lens which satisfies SLM manufacture with coaxial 532 nm and 1030 nm~1080 nm laser beams. It is composed of three pieces of spherical lenses. The focal spots for 532 nm laser and 1030 nm~1080 nm laser are smaller than 35 μm and 70 μm, respectively. The results meet the demands of high precision SLM. The chromatic aberration could cause separation between two laser focal spots in the scanning plane, so chromatic aberration correction is very important to our design. The lateral color of the designed f-theta lens is less than 11 μm within the scan area of 150 mm x 150 mm, which meet the application requirements of dual wavelength selective laser melting.
